tiers.do: Brush your teeth with your other hand tonight.
tiers.why: Your hands have a hierarchy you never chose. Break it for ninety seconds.
tiers.alt: Unlock and scroll your phone with your other hand for five minutes.
tiers.when: I put my toothbrush back down tonight
tiers.open: Pick the brush up with the wrong hand before you think about it.
tiers.done: your teeth are clean and the other hand never took over.
tiers.test: to make a mess of it and give up halfway through.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Sit in a different chair for one meal.
tiers.why: Every room you own has an assigned seat. Nobody assigned it.
tiers.alt: Eat one meal standing at a window instead of where you always sit.
tiers.when: I put my plate in the sink this evening
tiers.open: Put your plate down somewhere other than your usual place.
tiers.done: you have eaten a whole meal from the other chair.
tiers.test: to find it uncomfortable and move back before you finish.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: End your shower with thirty seconds of cold.
tiers.why: Small, unpleasant, entirely reversible. Chosen discomfort behaves differently.
tiers.alt: Wash your hands and face in cold water for one full minute.
tiers.when: I turn the shower off
tiers.open: Turn the dial to cold while you are still under it.
tiers.done: thirty seconds of cold have passed and you turned it off, not warm again.
tiers.test: to gasp, panic, and turn it straight back to hot.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Do your morning routine in reverse order.
tiers.why: Sequence is habit wearing a disguise.
tiers.alt: Get dressed in a different order than you always do.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Do the last thing in your routine first, before you can think about it.
tiers.done: the whole routine is done and the order was genuinely reversed.
tiers.test: to get muddled, miss something, and be late.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Put your phone in another room for one hour while awake.
tiers.why: An hour of being unreachable is a starting dose.
tiers.alt: Leave your phone behind on one short errand today.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Take your phone into another room and put it face down.
tiers.done: an hour has passed and you did not go and get it.
tiers.test: to miss something urgent and for it to matter.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Eat something you have never eaten. One bite counts, and it can come from your own kitchen.
tiers.why: One bite. This is a data point, not a meal.
tiers.alt: Buy one unfamiliar item on your next shop and taste it.
tiers.when: I put my plate in the sink this evening
tiers.open: Open the cupboard and take out the thing you have never opened.
tiers.done: one bite of something you had never eaten is swallowed.
tiers.test: to find it disgusting and to have wasted food.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Listen to a full album from a genre you dislike.
tiers.why: You decided that years ago with less information.
tiers.alt: Watch twenty minutes of a sport or show you would never pick.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Put the album on and sit down before the first track ends.
tiers.done: the album has played to the end without being skipped.
tiers.test: to hate it within two tracks and resent the time.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Take a ten-minute walk with no audio in your ears.
tiers.why: Silence is a stimulus you have been filtering out.
tiers.alt: Sit for ten minutes with nothing playing and nothing to read.
tiers.when: I put my shoes on tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Leave the headphones on the table, not in your pocket.
tiers.done: ten minutes outside are done with nothing in your ears.
tiers.test: to be bored, and for your own thoughts to be unpleasant company.
tiers.stop: No headphones. Hearing the place is part of it.

tiers.do: Write one page by hand about anything.
tiers.why: Slower thinking produces different thoughts.
tiers.alt: Write half a page by hand — a list, a letter, a complaint.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Find paper and a pen and write the first line, however bad.
tiers.done: one full page is covered in your handwriting.
tiers.test: to have nothing to say and stare at the paper.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Spend twenty minutes on a skill you have never touched.
tiers.why: Being bad at something new is the only entry fee. Pay it early.
tiers.alt: Watch one tutorial and attempt the first step, badly.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Open the first tutorial and do only what it shows in the first minute.
tiers.done: twenty minutes have gone on something your hands have never done.
tiers.test: to be hopeless at it and feel too old to be starting.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Cook one thing without a recipe.
tiers.why: Improvisation fails cheaply in a kitchen. Good place to practise.
tiers.alt: Change three things about a dish you make from memory.
tiers.when: I switch the kettle on after coming in
tiers.open: Open the fridge and take out three things without deciding anything.
tiers.done: something edible exists and no recipe was consulted.
tiers.test: to ruin it and have to throw it away and start again.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Move your body for twenty minutes in a way it does not know.
tiers.why: Your body has a small vocabulary. Twenty minutes is one new word.
tiers.alt: Try five minutes each of four movements you never do.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Clear two square metres of floor and get into the middle of it.
tiers.done: twenty minutes of a movement your body does not know are behind you.
tiers.test: to look ridiculous and feel your body refuse.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Read ten pages of a book from a section you never browse.
tiers.why: Your reading has a shape. Step outside it for ten pages.
tiers.alt: Read one long article on a subject you know nothing about.
tiers.when: I finish eating lunch tomorrow
tiers.open: Open the book at page one and read to the bottom of it.
tiers.done: ten pages from a section you never browse are read.
tiers.test: to find it impenetrable and give up on page two.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Go a full day without your usual comfort — coffee, sugar, scrolling.
tiers.why: One day tells you whether it is a preference or a leash.
tiers.alt: Go half a day without the thing you reach for automatically.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Move the thing out of reach before you want it.
tiers.done: a full day has passed without it and you did not break at the end.
tiers.test: to be irritable, useless, and worse company all day.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Make something with your hands in under an hour.
tiers.why: Producing an object, however crude, changes your self-report.
tiers.alt: Repair something instead of replacing it.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Get the materials out and put them on the table where you will trip over them.
tiers.done: an object exists that did not exist this morning, however crude.
tiers.test: to make something embarrassing and want to hide it.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Do the thing you always do — somewhere you have never done it.
tiers.why: Same act, new context. Your routine is more portable than it feels.
tiers.alt: Work, read, or eat somewhere entirely unfamiliar today.
tiers.when: I put my bag down at home
tiers.open: Pack the one thing you need to do it and leave the house with it.
tiers.done: the usual thing is done, and it was done somewhere you had never done it.
tiers.test: to be unable to concentrate and get nothing done.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Learn ten words of a language you do not speak.
tiers.why: Ten words is nothing. Ten words is also how it starts.
tiers.alt: Learn to introduce yourself in an unfamiliar language.
tiers.when: I finish eating lunch tomorrow
tiers.open: Open a list of ten words and say the first one out loud.
tiers.done: you can say all ten words without looking.
tiers.test: to forget them within a day and prove you cannot learn languages.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Spend an evening with no screens at all.
tiers.why: Find out what you do when there is nothing to watch.
tiers.alt: Spend two hours with every screen off and out of sight.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Put every screen in a drawer and shut it.
tiers.done: the evening is over and no screen was switched on.
tiers.test: to be bored out of your mind and go to bed at nine.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Practise your new skill for thirty minutes, three days running.
tiers.why: Repetition is where novelty becomes capability.
tiers.alt: Practise fifteen minutes a day for three days.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Put the thirty minutes in your calendar for all three days, now.
tiers.done: three consecutive days each contain thirty minutes of practice.
tiers.test: to manage one day and quietly drop the other two.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Fix or build something you would normally pay someone to handle.
tiers.why: Outsourced competence is competence you do not have.
tiers.alt: Attempt one repair you would usually avoid.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find out what the repair needs and order the one part.
tiers.done: the thing works, or you know exactly why it does not.
tiers.test: to break it worse and have to pay someone anyway.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Wake ninety minutes earlier and use the time deliberately.
tiers.why: The hour before the day starts belongs to nobody else.
tiers.alt: Wake an hour earlier and do one thing that matters to you.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Set the alarm ninety minutes early and write down what the time is for.
tiers.done: you were awake ninety minutes early and used the time as written.
tiers.test: to lie awake, be exhausted all day, and waste the hour anyway.
tiers.stop: Not when you feel readier. Today's version is the task.

tiers.do: Take a physical class you have never taken. One session.
tiers.why: Turning up as a visible beginner is the actual exercise.
tiers.alt: Follow a full beginner session at home, start to finish.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one class, one date, and book the single session.
tiers.done: you turned up, stayed the whole session, and were visibly the beginner.
tiers.test: to be the worst in the room and for everyone to notice.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Cook a dish from a cuisine you have never cooked. Badly is acceptable.
tiers.why: Inedible still counts. The technique is the point, not dinner.
tiers.alt: Cook one unfamiliar dish from written instructions only.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Write the shopping list for the dish before you look up a technique.
tiers.done: the dish was cooked from written instructions. Edible is optional.
tiers.test: to produce something inedible and have wasted the ingredients.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend two hours making something you will show nobody.
tiers.why: Work with no audience is where taste develops.
tiers.alt: Make something for an hour with no intention of keeping it.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Set a timer for two hours and start before you decide what it is.
tiers.done: two hours are gone and nobody has seen it or will.
tiers.test: to make something worthless and feel the two hours were wasted.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Do one physical movement until your form breaks, then stop.
tiers.why: Form failure is a real, visible limit and a safe one. Exhaustion is neither, which is why it is not the instruction.
tiers.alt: Push one exercise to the point the technique goes, and stop there.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Pick one movement and do the first set properly.
tiers.done: you stopped at the point your form broke, not before and not after.
tiers.test: to fail early, in front of yourself, well short of anything impressive.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Change one daily habit and hold it for a week.
tiers.why: Seven days is where a change stops being an experiment.
tiers.alt: Hold one small change for five consecutive days.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Write the one change on a card and put it where the old habit happens.
tiers.done: seven consecutive days contain the change, with no day missed.
tiers.test: to break on day three and prove the whole method does not work.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Learn to do one useful thing you have always avoided.
tiers.why: Avoidance compounds. So does competence.
tiers.alt: Learn the first stage of the thing you keep avoiding.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Name the thing you have avoided. Open one page about how to start it.
tiers.done: you can do the thing, badly, without help.
tiers.test: to find out there was a good reason you avoided it.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Spend a full day doing only things you did not plan.
tiers.why: Improvised days teach you what you actually want to do.
tiers.alt: Leave half a day entirely unplanned and follow impulses.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Cancel or clear the day. That is the whole first move.
tiers.done: a full day has passed with nothing in it that you planned.
tiers.test: to waste the day entirely and feel worse at the end of it.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Read a whole book in a field you know nothing about.
tiers.why: Depth in an unfamiliar area is how the map grows outward.
tiers.alt: Finish a short book or long report on an unfamiliar subject.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Get the book and read the first page tonight.
tiers.done: the book is finished, cover to cover.
tiers.test: to lose interest at a third of the way in and abandon it.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Give up one comfort for a full week.
tiers.why: A week without it tells you exactly what it was doing for you.
tiers.alt: Give up one habit for four days running.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Remove it from the house, or put it somewhere you cannot reach.
tiers.done: seven days have passed without it, with no exceptions made.
tiers.test: to cave by the third day and feel it proves something about you.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Attend one in-person session of a class. Any class.
tiers.why: A room of strangers, all better than you. That is the tier.
tiers.alt: Attend any free public workshop, talk, or open session.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one session happening this week and put your name down.
tiers.done: you were in the room for a full session of something.
tiers.test: to be out of place, underprepared, and clearly the weakest there.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Practise your skill for six hours across one week.
tiers.why: Volume, not inspiration. Book the hours.
tiers.alt: Practise four hours across one week, logged honestly.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Book the six hours into the week as six separate appointments.
tiers.done: six hours of practice are logged across one week, honestly counted.
tiers.test: to manage two hours and lie to yourself about the rest.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Make something to a deadline you set out loud.
tiers.why: Announced deadlines behave differently to private ones.
tiers.alt: Tell one person what you will finish, and by when.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Say the deadline out loud to one person, with the date in it.
tiers.done: the thing is finished, by the date you said out loud.
tiers.test: to miss the date and have someone know you missed it.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Do a physical activity that scares you slightly.
tiers.why: Slight fear is the correct dose at this tier.
tiers.alt: Do the physical thing you have been calling 'not for me'.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the thing that scares you slightly and book it for a specific day.
tiers.done: you did it, and the slight fear was present the whole time.
tiers.test: to freeze on the day, or to be hurt doing it.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Spend a whole day learning one thing, start to finish.
tiers.why: Immersion beats scheduling. Give it eight hours.
tiers.alt: Spend four uninterrupted hours on a single skill.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Block eight hours tomorrow and name the one thing in the calendar entry.
tiers.done: eight hours have gone on one thing, start to finish, in one day.
tiers.test: to burn out by hour three and have nothing to show.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Cook for someone else. Something you have never made.
tiers.why: Another person eating it raises the stakes correctly.
tiers.alt: Make something unfamiliar and give it to one person.
tiers.when: I finish eating lunch tomorrow
tiers.open: Ask one person when they are free to eat. Nothing else yet.
tiers.done: someone else has eaten something you had never made before.
tiers.test: for it to be bad and for them to have to be polite about it.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Take a full day off from every obligation, with nothing scheduled.
tiers.why: Rest is a skill and you are probably bad at it.
tiers.alt: Take half a day fully off, phone silenced, nothing planned.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Put the day in the calendar as blocked and silence your phone for it.
tiers.done: a day has passed with no obligation met and nothing scheduled.
tiers.test: to be restless, guilty, and unable to actually rest.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Learn a piece, routine, or sequence by heart.
tiers.why: Memorised skill lives in the body. Nothing else does.
tiers.alt: Learn a short sequence well enough to do it without prompts.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Learn the opening four bars or movements only.
tiers.done: you can do the whole sequence through with no prompts.
tiers.test: to forget it halfway and realise you cannot hold anything in your head.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Do the same unfamiliar activity three times in one week.
tiers.why: The third time is when your opinion of it becomes real.
tiers.alt: Repeat one new activity three times, however short.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Put the three dates in this week now, before you do it once.
tiers.done: the same unfamiliar activity has happened three times inside one week.
tiers.test: to do it once, hate it, and skip the other two.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Show your work to one person who will be honest.
tiers.why: Honest feedback is the fastest route to capable.
tiers.alt: Ask one person for one specific criticism of your work.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Choose the person who will not be kind about it and send one message.
tiers.done: one honest person has seen your work and told you something true.
tiers.test: to be told it is bad in a way you cannot recover from.
tiers.stop: Nobody present who already likes you.
tiers.say: "I want the real version, not the encouraging one."

tiers.do: Spend a month doing twenty minutes a day on one skill.
tiers.why: Thirty days of small is how capability is actually built.
tiers.alt: Twenty minutes a day for three weeks.
tiers.when: I put my toothbrush back down tonight
tiers.open: Put the twenty minutes at the same time every day, starting tonight.
tiers.done: thirty consecutive days each contain twenty minutes.
tiers.test: to miss a few days, lose the chain, and quietly stop.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Perform the skill in front of exactly one person.
tiers.why: One witness converts a hobby into something with stakes.
tiers.alt: Record yourself doing it and send it to one person.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Ask one person to watch for five minutes. Do not explain why.
tiers.done: one person has watched you do the thing, live.
tiers.test: to go to pieces with someone watching and be humiliated.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Take a full weekend course in something unrelated to your life.
tiers.why: Two days of being a beginner among beginners.
tiers.alt: Do a full-day intensive in something entirely new.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the course, check the date, pay the deposit.
tiers.done: two full days of being a beginner are behind you.
tiers.test: to be the least able person there for two whole days.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Do something physical harder than anything you did last year.
tiers.why: Beat last year's best. That is the whole measure.
tiers.alt: Set and beat a personal physical record.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Write down last year's best number. That is what you are beating.
tiers.done: this year's number is higher than the one you wrote down.
tiers.test: to fall short of last year and find out you are declining.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Sell, publish, or submit something you made.
tiers.why: Putting work into the world where it can be rejected.
tiers.alt: Submit one piece of work somewhere it will be judged.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one place that accepts submissions and open the form.
tiers.done: the work has been sent, sold or submitted somewhere real.
tiers.test: to be rejected, and for the rejection to be the final word.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.

tiers.do: Spend a week without the thing you use to avoid boredom.
tiers.why: Boredom is where new activities come from. Let it in.
tiers.alt: Five days with your main distraction removed.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Delete it, or hand the device to someone else for the week.
tiers.done: seven days have passed with no access to it at all.
tiers.test: to be unbearably bored and to find out you have no interests.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Learn enough of a practical skill to help someone with it.
tiers.why: Useful is the threshold that separates hobby from capability.
tiers.alt: Learn one skill well enough to do it for someone else.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Learn the one part someone would actually need from you.
tiers.done: you have used the skill to help another person with a real problem.
tiers.test: to get it wrong and make someone else's situation worse.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Do an activity alone that you have only ever done with others.
tiers.why: Alone removes the social scaffolding. What is left is yours.
tiers.alt: Go to a cinema, restaurant, or event alone.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Book one ticket, not two.
tiers.done: you have done it alone, start to finish, without arranging company.
tiers.test: to be visibly alone and pitied for it.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Train for something with a fixed date you cannot move.
tiers.why: An immovable date rearranges everything around it, correctly.
tiers.alt: Commit to a dated event and start the preparation this week.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the dated event and enter it today, while the date is still far away.
tiers.done: the date arrived and you were prepared enough to turn up.
tiers.test: to be unprepared on the day and to have paid to be humiliated.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Spend a weekend building one finished thing.
tiers.why: Finished, not started. That distinction is the whole tier.
tiers.alt: Take something half-done and finish it completely.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Pick the one thing and write down what finished looks like.
tiers.done: one thing is finished. Not improved, not nearly — finished.
tiers.test: to get it to ninety per cent and leave it there like the others.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Enter a public arena — open mic, jam night, tournament, showcase.
tiers.why: Strangers who did not choose to watch you. That is the escalation.
tiers.alt: Perform or compete in any setting open to the public.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the open mic, jam or tournament and put your name on the list.
tiers.done: you performed or competed in front of people who did not choose to watch you.
tiers.test: to be bad in front of strangers and for it to be visibly awkward.
tiers.stop: Nobody present who already likes you.

tiers.do: Ask a practitioner to critique your work in person.
tiers.why: Someone better than you, looking closely, saying true things.
tiers.alt: Get direct feedback from someone genuinely skilled.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one practitioner near you and send one message asking for an hour.
tiers.done: someone better than you has looked closely and said true things.
tiers.test: to be told the work is not worth continuing.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "Would you look at this and tell me what is wrong with it?"

tiers.do: Do the physical thing you assumed your body could not do.
tiers.why: That assumption was never tested. Test it.
tiers.alt: Attempt the physical goal you had written off.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Write down the physical thing you had ruled out. Book the first session.
tiers.done: you attempted the thing your body was supposedly not for.
tiers.test: to be physically unable, publicly, and to have the assumption confirmed.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Spend a month with one form of media entirely cut out.
tiers.why: Thirty days of not consuming it. Notice what fills the space.
tiers.alt: Cut one media habit completely for three weeks.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Remove the apps or cancel the subscription tonight.
tiers.done: a month has passed with that form of media entirely absent.
tiers.test: to be out of the loop, bored, and to have missed something that mattered.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Compete where results are recorded and public.
tiers.why: A recorded outcome you cannot quietly forget.
tiers.alt: Enter anything with published results, however small.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the event with published results and enter it.
tiers.done: your result is recorded somewhere you cannot quietly delete.
tiers.test: to come last, in public, with the number permanently attached to your name.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Learn a second skill from scratch while keeping the first.
tiers.why: Two beginnings at once. Harder, and it proves the method.
tiers.alt: Start a second unfamiliar skill alongside your current one.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Put the second skill in the calendar without removing the first.
tiers.done: both skills have had real hours this week, neither abandoned.
tiers.test: to lose the first skill while being bad at the second.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Make something and give it away to a stranger.
tiers.why: Made, released, no credit. Good for the ego and the craft.
tiers.alt: Give something you made to someone who did not ask for it.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Make the thing first. Decide who gets it afterwards.
tiers.done: something you made is in a stranger's hands and your name is not on it.
tiers.test: for them not to want it, and to be embarrassed offering it.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Spend a full day in silence.
tiers.why: A day without speaking rearranges how you listen.
tiers.alt: Spend half a day without speaking to anyone.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Tell the people you live or work with before you start.
tiers.done: a full day has passed without you speaking.
tiers.test: to be unable to manage it and to look foolish for announcing it.
tiers.stop: Do not announce it first. Announcing it is not doing it.

tiers.do: Do a week where every day contains one unfamiliar act.
tiers.why: Seven consecutive firsts. Novelty as a daily practice.
tiers.alt: Five consecutive days, one new thing each day.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write seven lines in your notes tonight. One unfamiliar act per day.
tiers.done: seven consecutive days each contain one thing you had never done.
tiers.test: to run out of ideas by day four and let the week collapse.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Take on a project you are not qualified for.
tiers.why: Competence arrives during the work, not before it.
tiers.alt: Say yes to something slightly beyond your current ability.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Say yes to the thing you are not qualified for, in writing, today.
tiers.done: the project is delivered, and you were under-qualified when you started.
tiers.test: to be found out mid-project and let someone down badly.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Commit to a six-week course with attendance you cannot quietly drop.
tiers.why: Six weeks outlasts enthusiasm. That is why it is on the list.
tiers.alt: Commit to six weeks of anything with other people expecting you.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Pay for the six weeks up front so dropping it costs something.
tiers.done: all six weeks were attended, including the ones where you did not want to go.
tiers.test: to drop out around week three and be the person who left.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Train four days a week for a month.
tiers.why: Consistency at this density changes the body and the self-image.
tiers.alt: Train three days a week for a month without missing.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Put four sessions a week in the calendar for the whole month, now.
tiers.done: four sessions a week for a month, with none quietly dropped.
tiers.test: to miss a week, lose the rhythm, and stop pretending.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Perform or present to a room of more than twenty people.
tiers.why: Twenty faces is the tier where the voice starts to shake. Continue anyway.
tiers.alt: Speak or perform to the largest group you can arrange.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the room of twenty and ask for a slot.
tiers.done: you spoke or performed in front of more than twenty people.
tiers.test: for your voice to go, your mind to go blank, and the room to see it.
tiers.stop: Nobody present who already likes you.

tiers.do: Spend a month building one substantial thing.
tiers.why: Thirty days on one object. Depth over variety, for once.
tiers.alt: Three weeks on a single significant project.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Define what the one thing is in a single sentence tonight.
tiers.done: a month has gone into one object and the object exists.
tiers.test: to lose interest at week two and have a half-built thing.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Take a skill you are mediocre at and get measurably better.
tiers.why: Measurable. Write the number down before you start.
tiers.alt: Pick one measurable ability and improve it by a stated amount.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Write down the number you are at now, before you start.
tiers.done: the number you wrote down has gone up measurably.
tiers.test: to measure it and find no improvement at all after all that work.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Do the thing you have been saying you will do 'one day'.
tiers.why: One day has been doing a lot of work for you. Retire it.
tiers.alt: Take the first irreversible step on the 'one day' thing.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Name the 'one day' thing out loud. Do the first part of it that costs something.
tiers.done: the thing you kept saying you would do one day is done.
tiers.test: to do it and find it was never worth all the waiting.
tiers.stop: Not when you feel readier. Today's version is the task.

tiers.do: Join a group where everyone is better than you and stay a month.
tiers.why: Being the worst in the room is the fastest classroom there is.
tiers.alt: Train or work with people clearly above your level for a month.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the group where you will be the worst and turn up once.
tiers.done: a month has passed in a room where you were the least able person.
tiers.test: to be unwelcome, slow, and a drag on everyone else.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Spend two months on a skill with a public end point.
tiers.why: A date, an audience, and no way to quietly reschedule.
tiers.alt: Eight weeks of preparation toward one public outcome.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Name the public end point and put the date in writing.
tiers.done: the date came and you presented, performed or delivered.
tiers.test: to get there unready and fail in front of the people you told.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Break a routine you have held for over five years.
tiers.why: Five years is long enough that it stopped being a decision.
tiers.alt: Change one long-standing routine for a full month.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write down the routine you have held for five years. Tonight is the last night of it.
tiers.done: a month has passed without the routine you held for five years.
tiers.test: to lose something load-bearing and come apart without it.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Make something in public, where people can watch you fail.
tiers.why: Working in view removes the option of quietly abandoning it.
tiers.alt: Share your work in progress publicly, unfinished.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Set up where people can see you and start before you are ready.
tiers.done: you worked where people could watch, including the parts that went wrong.
tiers.test: to be watched failing and have no way to hide it.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Compete or perform monthly for three months.
tiers.why: Repetition under exposure. This is where nerve becomes normal.
tiers.alt: Three public outings in three months, however small.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Book all three dates now, across three months.
tiers.done: three public outings happened in three months, however small.
tiers.test: to do the first and find excuses for the other two.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Learn a skill in a language or setting not your own.
tiers.why: Two unfamiliar things at once. It compounds faster than you expect.
tiers.alt: Learn something taught in an unfamiliar language or culture.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the teacher, class or setting that is not in your language.
tiers.done: you learned the thing in a setting that was not yours.
tiers.test: to understand nothing and waste the money.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Take a qualification, grading, or examination in your new skill.
tiers.why: An external standard, externally judged. No self-marking.
tiers.alt: Submit to any formal assessment of your ability.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the qualification, check the date, pay the entry.
tiers.done: you sat the assessment and the result is external and recorded.
tiers.test: to fail it and have the failure be official.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Spend three months training for one physical goal.
tiers.why: Ninety days pointed at one outcome. Nothing else needs to change.
tiers.alt: Ten weeks of structured training toward one target.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write down the one goal and the date. Then the first week's sessions.
tiers.done: three months of structured training are behind you, pointed at one thing.
tiers.test: to get injured, or bored, and abandon it in month two.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Do something creative every day for a month and show all of it.
tiers.why: Thirty pieces, all visible, including the bad ones.
tiers.alt: Make and share something daily for three weeks.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Make the first thing tonight and post it before you judge it.
tiers.done: thirty days of work are made and all of it is visible, including the bad.
tiers.test: to post something embarrassing and for people to see it.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Take on a paid job in your new skill.
tiers.why: Money changes the relationship. Somebody now expects quality.
tiers.alt: Do your new skill for someone in exchange for something real.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Name a price out loud to one person who might pay it.
tiers.done: someone paid you for the skill and received what they paid for.
tiers.test: to charge for something you are not good enough at and be found out.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Spend a month living without one thing you consider essential.
tiers.why: Essential is a strong word. Audit it for thirty days.
tiers.alt: Three weeks without the thing you call non-negotiable.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Remove the essential thing from the house today.
tiers.done: a month has passed without the thing you called non-negotiable.
tiers.test: to discover you genuinely needed it and that the month damaged something.
tiers.stop: No easier version first to warm up with.

tiers.do: Enter something where you will very likely place last.
tiers.why: Placing last still clears the tier. Showing up is the entire ask.
tiers.alt: Enter a field where you are plainly outmatched.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Enter the field where you are clearly outmatched. Pay the entry today.
tiers.done: you turned up and completed it, whatever the placing.
tiers.test: to come last by a humiliating margin.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Build something that solves a real problem for someone else.
tiers.why: Useful to another person is the highest form of capable.
tiers.alt: Make something specifically for one person's actual problem.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Ask one person what their actual problem is. Write it down.
tiers.done: someone else's real problem is solved by something you built.
tiers.test: to build the wrong thing and waste their time as well as yours.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Teach the thing you were useless at eighty days ago.
tiers.why: Teaching is the audit. You cannot fake it in front of a beginner.
tiers.alt: Show one person how to start the skill you have built.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Find one beginner and offer one hour.
tiers.done: a beginner can now do the first part because of you.
tiers.test: to be exposed as not actually understanding it.
tiers.stop: Do not look it up beforehand. Arrive uninformed.

tiers.do: Run a workshop, class, or session for a group.
tiers.why: A room expecting you to know things. You do now.
tiers.alt: Teach a small group, however informally.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Pick the date, name the session, and tell the first person.
tiers.done: a group turned up and you ran the session end to end.
tiers.test: to lose the room, be asked something you cannot answer, and stall.
tiers.stop: Nobody present who already likes you.

tiers.do: Spend three months on a project with a public deadline.
tiers.why: Ninety days, announced. The announcement is half the work.
tiers.alt: Ten weeks toward something you have publicly committed to.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Announce the deadline publicly tonight, with the date.
tiers.done: ninety days ended with the thing delivered on the announced date.
tiers.test: to miss the public deadline and have it be visible.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Do the physical challenge you thought was for other people.
tiers.why: Other people were never a different species.
tiers.alt: Attempt the physical event you had ruled out entirely.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Enter the event you had ruled out as being for other people.
tiers.done: you were at the start line of the thing you thought was not for you.
tiers.test: to not finish, and for that to prove you were right to rule it out.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Rebuild your week from scratch around what you now do.
tiers.why: Your calendar still reflects who you were ninety days ago.
tiers.alt: Redesign your week around your new capabilities.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Open your calendar and delete one standing commitment that no longer fits.
tiers.done: your week is rebuilt around what you do now, not what you did.
tiers.test: to dismantle a week that was holding you up and have nothing replace it.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Take on an apprenticeship, mentorship, or serious study.
tiers.why: Submit to someone else's standard for a sustained period.
tiers.alt: Commit to a long-term learning relationship with an expert.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one person worth learning from and send one honest message.
tiers.done: you are under someone else's standard, with a schedule you did not set.
tiers.test: to be rejected, or accepted and then found inadequate.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.

tiers.do: Make something that will outlast your interest in it.
tiers.why: Build past the enthusiasm. That is what finishing means.
tiers.alt: Finish something after the excitement has fully worn off.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write down the finish condition tonight, while you still care.
tiers.done: the thing is finished, and it was finished after the interest ran out.
tiers.test: to lose interest and have the unfinished thing sit there as evidence.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Compete at the highest level you can currently access.
tiers.why: Find your actual ceiling. It is higher and lower than you think.
tiers.alt: Enter the strongest field that will accept you.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the strongest field that will accept you and enter it.
tiers.done: you competed at the highest level currently open to you.
tiers.test: to be comprehensively out of your depth and know it publicly.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Spend six months developing one capability seriously.
tiers.why: Half a year. This is where amateurs become practitioners.
tiers.alt: Five months of sustained, structured practice.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write the six-month plan on one page. Then book this week.
tiers.done: six months of serious, structured work are behind you.
tiers.test: to plateau at month three and find out you have a ceiling.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Do something publicly that could genuinely embarrass you.
tiers.why: Survivable embarrassment is the cheapest freedom available.
tiers.alt: Take a public risk with real potential to go badly.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Choose the public thing that could genuinely embarrass you. Commit today.
tiers.done: the embarrassing thing happened in public and you are still here.
tiers.test: to be humiliated in a way people remember and bring up.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Enter something you can publicly and visibly fail at.
tiers.why: Recorded, ranked, witnessed. Placing last still clears it.
tiers.alt: Enter any event where the result is public and final.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the event with a final, public result and enter it.
tiers.done: the result is public, final, and has your name on it.
tiers.test: to fail visibly, permanently, and on the record.
tiers.stop: Do not film it or photograph it. No proof, no audience.

tiers.do: Take a real risk with your work — leave, launch, or ask.
tiers.why: A risk with actual consequences. The rest was rehearsal.
tiers.alt: Make the professional move you have been deferring.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Write the email, the resignation or the ask. Do not send it yet — write it.
tiers.done: the real professional risk is taken, not deferred again.
tiers.test: for it to go wrong and cost you something you cannot replace.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.

tiers.do: Build something with someone whose standards exceed yours.
tiers.why: Collaboration with someone better is an accelerant and a mirror.
tiers.alt: Partner on a project with someone clearly more skilled.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Ask the person whose standards exceed yours for one hour of collaboration.
tiers.done: something exists that neither of you would have made alone.
tiers.test: to be the weak half and for them to regret agreeing.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Spend a year's worth of effort in three focused months.
tiers.why: Intensity is a variable most people never touch.
tiers.alt: Three months at the highest sustainable intensity.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write down what a year of this normally looks like. Compress it onto three months.
tiers.done: three months contained a year's worth of effort, honestly counted.
tiers.test: to burn out in week five and lose the rest of the year too.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Put your work in front of people who owe you nothing.
tiers.why: Strangers with no obligation to be kind. The only real test.
tiers.alt: Show your work to an audience with no personal connection.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the audience with no connection to you and put the work in front of them.
tiers.done: people who owe you nothing have seen the work and responded.
tiers.test: to be met with indifference, which is worse than criticism.
tiers.stop: Nobody present who already likes you.

tiers.do: Make the thing you have been afraid was beyond you.
tiers.why: The ceiling was self-installed. Take it down.
tiers.alt: Start the project you have called too ambitious.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write the thing you are afraid is beyond you on one line. Start the first part.
tiers.done: the thing you called beyond you exists.
tiers.test: to try it, fail, and have the ceiling turn out to be real.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Teach or lead a group through something difficult.
tiers.why: Responsibility for other people's progress, not just your own.
tiers.alt: Lead others through a challenge you have already cleared.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Pick the group and the difficult thing, and set the first date.
tiers.done: a group got through something hard and you led them through it.
tiers.test: for someone to be hurt or lost because you led badly.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Build a practice you will still be doing in ten years.
tiers.why: Design for the long run. Novelty was only the doorway.
tiers.alt: Establish one practice with a decade-long horizon.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Write the practice down as it would look in ten years. Do today's version.
tiers.done: the practice exists in a form you can still be doing in a decade.
tiers.test: to design something you abandon within the year like the others.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Stake something real on your capability.
tiers.why: Money, time, or reputation on the line. Skin in the game.
tiers.alt: Commit something you would genuinely miss to your own ability.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Name what you are staking and put it somewhere you cannot take it back.
tiers.done: something you would genuinely miss was staked on your own capability.
tiers.test: to lose it, and for the loss to prove the capability was not real.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Live a full month as the person you have been becoming.
tiers.why: Not practising it. Being it, for thirty consecutive days.
tiers.alt: Spend a month operating entirely as your new self.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Write down what that person's ordinary Tuesday looks like. Live today as it.
tiers.done: thirty consecutive days were lived as the person, not as practice.
tiers.test: to slip back within a week and find the whole thing was a costume.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Give up a defining routine for thirty days and replace it with what you built here.
tiers.why: You have spent ninety-nine tiers proving you are not your habits. This is where you prove it at the scale that matters — the routine you would have called part of your personality, gone, and the capability you built standing in its place.
tiers.alt: Replace your most defining habit with your new practice for a month.
tiers.when: I put my phone on charge for the night
tiers.open: Name the defining routine out loud. Tonight is the last night it runs.
tiers.done: thirty days have passed with the defining routine gone and the new practice in its place.
tiers.test: to lose the routine and find there was no person underneath it.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.
